(3) This section summarizes changes from third quarter of 2026 compared to second quarter of 2026, unless otherwise noted. • Third quarter results reflect the completion of the Regional Acceptance Corporation (RAC) loan sale and the subsequent AFS securities repositioning • Signed an agreement on October 14, 2026, to sell $7.7 billion of unsecured consumer loans representing substantially all assets of LightStream, our unsecured lending platform, to Carlyle Group Inc. • Adjusted net income available to common shareholders (1) of $1.4 billion, resulting in adjusted diluted EPS (1) of $1.16 per share and adjusted ROTCE (1) of 14.6%, which excludes: ◦ $1.4 billion pre-tax, or $0.90 per share, loss on the sale of AFS securities ◦ $581 million pre-tax, or $0.36 per share, loan loss reserve recapture and $106 million pre-tax, or $0.06 per share, of impacts associated with the RAC loan sale • Adjusted revenue - TE (1) of $5.3 billion was stable ◦ Net interest income - TE (1) increased 1.1%; NIM - TE (1) was up two basis points ◦ Noninterest income was impacted by losses on the RAC loan sale and the AFS securities repositioning, partially offset by record quarterly income for wealth management • Noninterest expense, excluding $40 million of RAC loan sale costs, was stable • End of period loans and leases HFI were $323.9 billion, down $5.9 billion, $5.5 billion of which was due to the RAC loan sale • End of period deposits were $413.2 billion, up $3.9 billion, or 0.9% • Asset quality improved as a result of the RAC loan sale ◦ NCO ratio of 77 basis points, which includes 39 basis points related to RAC ◦ Nonperforming loans to total loans HFI were 0.40%, down 11 basis points ◦ ALLL ratio of 1.25% declined 26 basis points ◦ Ratio of ALLL to nonperforming loans and leases HFI of 3.1x CEO Commentary “Since joining Truist, I’ve become even more confident in the strength of our franchise and the significant opportunities ahead. We delivered a solid quarter while also taking decisive actions to better position Truist for the future. These actions strengthen our risk, liquidity, and funding profile and create greater capacity to invest in our best businesses. We’re simplifying the company and focusing our resources, capital, and expenses on the businesses and capabilities that will help us become the most important financial partner to our clients. Looking ahead, we remain confident in our ability to deliver against our near- and long-term ROTCE targets and will work to build a more focused company positioned to deliver sustainable growth and stronger returns for shareholders.” — Mike Lyons, Truist President & CEO ` Contact: Investors: Brad Milsaps investors@truist.com Media: Kyle Tarrance media@truist.com Net Interest Income, Net Interest Margin, and Average Balances Quarter Ended Change (Dollars in millions) 3Q26 2Q26 3Q25 Link Quarter Like Quarter Interest income $ 6,030 $ 5,967 $ 6,286 $ 63 1.1 % $ (256) (4.1) % Plus: TE adjustment (1) 44 46 51 (2) (4.3) (7) (13.7) Interest income - TE (1) 6,074 6,013 6,337 61 1.0 (263) (4.2) Interest expense 2,367 2,346 2,657 21 0.9 (290) (10.9) Net interest income - TE (1) $ 3,707 $ 3,667 $ 3,680 $ 40 1.1 $ 27 0.7 NIM - TE (1) 3.00 % 2.98 % 3.01 % 2 bps (1) bp Average Balances (2) Total earning assets $ 491,430 $ 492,461 $ 486,006 $ (1,031) (0.2) % $ 5,424 1.1 % Total interest-bearing liabilities 371,474 370,782 359,103 692 0.2 12,371 3.4 Yields / Rates (1) Total earning assets 4.91 % 4.89 % 5.18 % 2 bps (27) bps Total interest-bearing liabilities 2.53 2.54 2.94 (1) bp (41) bps (1) Amounts related to interest income and yields are on a TE basis, which represents a non-GAAP measure, utilizing the federal income tax rate of 21% for the periods presented. reference.summary: Truist Financial Corporation, a financial services company, provides banking and trust services in the Southeastern and Mid-Atlantic United States. The company operates through two segments, Consumer and Small Business Banking; and Wholesale Banking. Its deposit products include noninterest-bearing checking, interest-bearing checking, savings, and money market deposit accounts, as well as certificates of deposit and individual retirement accounts. The company also provides funding; asset management; credit card lending; home equity and mortgage lending; other direct retail lending; home mortgage lending; Investment brokerage services; mobile/online banking; payment solutions; point-of-sale lending; retail and small business deposit products; and small business lending.
